title: Rutherford's atomic model and its limitations
topicTitle: Rutherford's atomic model and its limitations
notes: **Alpha-particle scattering.** Rutherford bombarded a thin gold foil with fast alpha particles and observed their deflection with a fluorescent screen — the experiment that revealed the nucleus.
**Observations.** Most alpha particles passed straight through, a few were deflected at large angles, and about one in 8000 bounced back, showing the positive charge and mass sit in a tiny core.
**Nuclear model.** The atom is mostly empty space: a dense, positively charged nucleus of about 10⁻¹⁵ m radius is surrounded by electrons moving in the remaining space (atom ~10⁻¹⁰ m).
**Limitation — stability.** By Maxwell's theory an orbiting electron radiates energy and should spiral into the nucleus in about 10⁻¹¹ s, so the model cannot explain atomic stability.
**Limitation — spectra.** The model predicts a continuous spectrum, but hydrogen emits a discrete line spectrum; it also could not explain the chemical behaviour of atoms.
